items.claim: The onset at 5:4 is byte-sound, but a pardon-verb catchword straddling the row's own front seam is undisclosed and the closing refrain is asserted with neither its sites nor a tier named.
items.evidence: Onset holds: וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי stands verse-initial at oshb:Jer.5.4 (byte tier), a 1cs qatal by its suffix, and both witnesses read the prophet's own report there. The ketiv/qere handling is exemplary - the source bytes at oshb:Jer.5.7 run אסלוח אֶֽסְלַֽח לָ֔ךְ, the unpointed ketiv immediately before the pointed qere, and the elided splice quotes the qere exactly as the row states. Undisclosed, however, is a byte-true device straddling the row's front seam: the same 1cs pardon verb closes oshb:Jer.5.1 as וְאֶסְלַ֖ח לָֽהּ and reopens at oshb:Jer.5.7 as אֶֽסְלַֽח לָ֔ךְ (both byte tier); the bare form is a 4-verse object book-wide (sweep: 4 verses) and stands at 2 verses inside this chapter, 5:1 and 5:7, so it argues cohesion of 5:1-5:9 against the cut at 5:4, and 5:1 is carried in no evidence ref. Second, the closing colon is called the refrain with no site and no tier: the object stands at 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses - 5:9, 5:29, and oshb:Jer.9.8 = web:Jer.9.9 inside the renumbered zone), and it is NOT identical across its two in-chapter sites at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier - oshb:Jer.5.9 reads הַֽעַל אֵ֥לֶּה לוֹא אֶפְקֹ֖ד נְאֻם יְהֹוָ֑ה וְאִם֙ against oshb:Jer.5.29 הַֽעַל אֵ֥לֶּה לֹֽא אֶפְקֹ֖ד נְאֻם יְהֹוָ֑ה אִ֚ם (plene negative and vav-prefixed conditional against defective and bare), a divergence both witnesses reflect; the shared tail is תִתְנַקֵּ֖ם נַפְשִֽׁי. Third, the closure signal keyed to 5:9 sits mid-verse there, unlike the verse-final tag at oshb:Jer.5.11. Minor: the opening splice is glossed at its tail alone, though the receiving translation supplied the rest.

items.claim: The byte claims verify, including the discipline that keeps the non-formulaic koh at 5:13 apart from the speech formula at 5:14.
items.evidence: עֲל֤וּ בְשָׁרוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ וְשַׁחֵ֔תוּ stands verse-initial at oshb:Jer.5.10 (byte tier) as a 2mp imperative pair, with the negative jussive וְכָלָ֖ה אַֽל תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ in the same verse - a discourse-frame imperative onset, and both witnesses render it so. Closure corroboration sits in the true postpositive position: the tag at oshb:Jer.5.11 is verse-final, unlike the mid-verse tags at 5:9, 5:15, 5:18 and 5:22. The quoted denial at oshb:Jer.5.12 carries its own speech verb, וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹא ה֑וּא (byte tier). The rejected alternative is byte-correct where it matters most: oshb:Jer.5.13 ends כֹּ֥ה יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה לָהֶֽם - a koh that is not a speech formula - and the row does not mistake it for the formula at 5:14. Setumah at 5:9 and at 5:13 are both disclosed under the correct type, single-witness and non-driving; the inventory records 0 ketiv/qere notes in this span; splice extent equals gloss extent. One item for the record rather than against the row: the negated make-a-full-end motif recurs past this row's back seam, וְכָלָ֖ה אַֽל תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ here against לֹֽא אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה אִתְּכֶ֖ם כָּלָֽה at oshb:Jer.5.18 (byte tier; bound collocations, sweep: 1 verse each - the bare token is a homograph set and carries no motif digit), and the Hebrew link goes unnamed on both sides of that seam.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah at 5:9 and 5:13, single-witness (row-disclosed, non-driving)

items.claim: The row files a 4-verse divine-title object under the 50-verse one its own bytes exclude it from, and leaves the make-a-full-end catchword crossing its front seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: The bytes at oshb:Jer.5.14 read כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֔וֹת (byte tier) - the Elohei stack, a distinct object standing at 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses - 5:14, 35:17, 38:17, 44:7). The substrate signal recorded for it is the plain armies-title, which as a speech formula stands at 50 verses (sweep: 50 verses) and byte-excludes 5:14, since the intervening אֱלֹהֵ֣י breaks the collocation; the plain form is what the bytes carry two units later at oshb:Jer.6.6 as יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת, so one signal key is doing duty for two byte-distinct title objects. Second, the row names 5:18-5:19 the not-a-full-end qualifier in English while its Hebrew twin sits across the row's own front seam: וְכָלָ֖ה אַֽל תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ at oshb:Jer.5.10 against לֹֽא אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה אִתְּכֶ֖ם כָּלָֽה at oshb:Jer.5.18 (byte tier; bound collocations, sweep: 1 verse each - the bare token is a homograph set, including the all-of-her form inside 6:6, and carries no motif digit), and both witnesses render both with the same English phrase. Third, the splice opens on לָכֵ֗ן, a backward-pointing connective binding the formula to the indictment it follows (sweep: 27 verses for that shape), quoted but not engaged by the restart characterisation. What holds: the formula is divine-mouthed and the frame owner does change across the seam, the people's denial at 5:12 giving way to divine speech at 5:14; setumah at 5:13 and 5:19 disclosed under the correct type; no ketiv/qere note in span; gloss parity exact.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah at 5:13 and 5:19, single-witness (row-disclosed, non-driving)

items.claim: The heuristic-false-positive disposition on the 5:24 ketiv/qere is refuted - the note rides on the exact lexeme the row's closing illustration is built from - and the row's own onset criterion is met unaddressed inside its span.
items.evidence: REFUTED. The inventory records a ketiv/qere note at oshb:Jer.5.24, and the bytes show why it is not incidental: the clause runs הַנֹּתֵ֗ן גֶּ֛שֶׁם וירה יוֹרֶ֥ה (byte tier), the unpointed ketiv standing immediately before the pointed qere, so the note rides on the early-rain noun itself - the very word the row's second illustration turns on, in the row's own closing verse. A span touching a ketiv/qere note owes disclosure, and this one is load-bearing rather than incidental; no row-level convention covers the omission, since disclosure is made at 5:6, 5:7 and 6:7 in the units flanking this one. Second, the row's stated onset criterion is met inside its own span and left unaddressed: oshb:Jer.5.21 opens שִׁמְעוּ נָ֣א זֹ֔את עַ֥ם סָכָ֖ל (byte tier), a 2mp imperative plus vocative - the same device class the row treats as onset-making at 5:20 - and the one byte that would subordinate it, the לֵאמֹֽר closing oshb:Jer.5.20, is the word the row's splice stops immediately before. Third, the declare-and-publish echo carries neither digit nor tier: the pairing is a 4-verse object (sweep: 4 verses - 4:5, 5:20, 46:14, 50:2) and the two forms differ, הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ at 4:5 against the vav-prefixed suffixed וְהַשְׁמִיע֥וּהָ at 5:20. Sound: the splice is byte tier with exact gloss parity, the setumah at 5:19 is disclosed and non-driving, and the refusal to cut where the receiving translation closes a quotation mark correctly treats that as apparatus rather than a Hebrew seam.

items.claim: Both splices, the addressee shift and the 1 in-span mark verify, and the row holds the soft internal seam open rather than cutting on topic alone.
items.evidence: עֲוֺנוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם הִטּוּ אֵ֑לֶּה stands verse-initial at oshb:Jer.5.25 (byte tier) with a 2mp suffix, and both witnesses read the turn to direct address; שַׁמָּה֙ וְשַׁ֣עֲרוּרָ֔ה נִהְיְתָ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ at oshb:Jer.5.30 is byte tier with exact gloss parity. Setumah at 5:29 is the span's 1 paragraph mark and is disclosed as internal, single-witness and non-driving; the inventory records 0 ketiv/qere notes in this span. The confidence posture is the right one: the closing capstone shows 0 imperative, vocative or speech-formula onsets in the bytes, and holding the unit whole at a hedged confidence with a bespoke rationale is preferable to cutting on topical development alone. Two items for the record rather than against the row. The refrain at 5:29 is named with neither site nor tier: the object stands at 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses - 5:9, 5:29, and oshb:Jer.9.8 = web:Jer.9.9, the third inside the renumbered zone, where any citation would owe a dual qualifier), and oshb:Jer.5.29 הַֽעַל אֵ֥לֶּה לֹֽא אֶפְקֹ֖ד נְאֻם יְהֹוָ֑ה אִ֚ם is not identical to oshb:Jer.5.9 הַֽעַל אֵ֥לֶּה לוֹא אֶפְקֹ֖ד נְאֻם יְהֹוָ֑ה וְאִם֙ at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier - defective negative and bare conditional against plene and vav-prefixed - a divergence both witnesses reflect. And the row's two closure signals converge on one verse, the refrain colon and the paragraph mark both falling at 5:29, which is the strongest available case for the split the row declines; the mark is disclosed but the convergence is not stated.

items.claim: The onset survives, but the cited echo is attributed to the wrong verse - the one other verse carrying the northern colon of 6:1 is 4:6, not 4:5 (sweep: 2 verses) - and the ground given for holding 6:2 with 6:3 is contradicted by both witnesses.
items.evidence: The quoted run הָעִ֣זוּ בְּנֵ֣י בִניָמִ֗ן מִקֶּ֨רֶב֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.6.1, byte tier) shares no consonantal word with the verse named as its echo source, which is the one of the two that the evidence refs carry. The echo attested in a sweep runs to oshb:Jer.4.6: the colon מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל is byte-identical at oshb:Jer.4.6 and oshb:Jer.6.1 and stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses), and the opening imperative is a mater-lectionis pair with that same verse - plene הָעִ֖יזוּ at 4:6 and defective הָעִ֣זוּ at 6:1 (sweep: 1 verse each spelling), the book's 2 occurrences of that imperative, in complementary spellings. The row's own prose quotes the very colon that duplicates 4:6 without disclosing the twin, and 4:6 is carried in no evidence ref; the one collocation 6:1 does share with the cited verse, תִּקְע֥וּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר, is not exclusive (sweep: 3 verses - 4:5, 6:1, 51:27) and is not in the quoted run at all. Second, the ground for holding 6:2 with 6:3 is that both continue in the same third-person descriptive mode: the finite verb at oshb:Jer.6.2 is דָּמִ֖יתִי (byte tier; sweep: 1 verse book-wide), a 1cs qatal by its suffix, and both witnesses read it as divine first-person speech - the third-person material is 6:3's יָבֹ֥אוּ רֹעִ֖ים וְעֶדְרֵיהֶ֑ם. Half the span being defended is misdescribed. The seam itself is undisturbed: הָעִ֣זוּ is a verse-initial imperative with בְּנֵ֣י בִניָמִ֗ן as vocative, a sufficient onset without any echo. For the record: the span carries 1 recorded seg, a paseq at 6:1 held as a count without a position, which goes unmentioned, though the row's negative statement is scoped to the paragraph layer and is accurate there.

items.claim: The quoted-speaker frame is grounded in the right bytes - the 1cp cohortative and the 1cp cry, not the imperatives alone - and the mark and quote claims verify.
items.evidence: קַדְּשׁ֤וּ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה ק֖וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה בַֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם at oshb:Jer.6.4 is byte tier with exact gloss parity. The frame claim does not rest on the imperatives, which would not distinguish the speaker from the summoning voice of 6:1: the 1cp cohortative וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה and the 1cp א֥וֹי לָ֨נוּ֙ fix the voice as the attacking force, and both witnesses read them so. The pair's internal binding is byte-true - ק֚וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה repeats at 6:4 and oshb:Jer.6.5 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide) - though the row argues that repetition only through the receiving translation. Setumah at 6:5 is disclosed under the correct type as own-closing, single-witness and non-driving; the inventory records 0 ketiv/qere notes in this span. Two observations rather than defects. The א֥וֹי at 6:4 belongs to the alas lexeme, not the woe-onset particle, and the row makes no device claim on it - correctly declining the blend. And the front seam carries continuity the row does not disclose: עָלֶ֤יהָ stands in both oshb:Jer.6.3 (תָּקְע֨וּ עָלֶ֤יהָ אֹהָלִים֙) and oshb:Jer.6.4 (קַדְּשׁ֤וּ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה) with the same referent, and the bytes carry 0 speech-onset markers at that seam, so the reported-speech reading rests on the person-marking alone. That reading is sound, but the absence of a quotation frame in the Hebrew belongs on the record.

items.claim: No byte claim is false and the seam stands, but the gloss set beside the splice covers neither end of what was spliced, and the formula the warrant rests on is a subordinated clause quoted without being engaged.
items.evidence: The splice at oshb:Jer.6.6 is byte tier and reads כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת כִּרְת֣וּ עֵצָ֔ה, but the English set beside it drops the four-word formula opening the splice and adds material the splice does not contain, וְשִׁפְכ֥וּ עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סֹלְלָ֑ה. Gloss extent must equal splice extent, and the part left unglossed is precisely the formula the whole warrant rests on. Second, that formula is subordinated: the splice's own first word is כִּ֣י, a causal connective, against the bare verse-initial כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת three verses later at oshb:Jer.6.9; the two shapes are separate objects book-wide (sweep: 29 verses carrying the subordinated shape, 153 verses carrying the formula at all), and the row calls it a restart without engaging the connective it quotes. Third, the frame-owner change that actually makes 6:6 an onset - the besiegers' cry at 6:4-6:5 giving way to divine speech - is the row's real ground and is left implicit; a formula warrant owes the mouth. What verifies: the ketiv/qere at 6:7 is disclosed without being quoted and the bytes bear it out, בור בַּ֨יִר֙ (unpointed ketiv immediately before pointed qere); setumah at 6:5 and petuchah at 6:8 are both disclosed under their own types, kept apart; and the internal-imperative reading of 6:8 is byte-sound - הִוָּסְרִי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם is a 2fs imperative naming the same city the splice's continuation names at 6:6, so the same-addressee, no-fresh-formula ground holds.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah at 6:5 (setumah) and 6:8 (petuchah), single-witness (row-disclosed, non-driving)
